items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] How about Sam Butera with Louis Prima? [INTERVIEWEE] Not at that time, nope, no.

ctx.x: saxophone player, Rebel Rouser. Then there were the little crossover things, as I know now, like Walkin’ with Mr. Lee, Lee Allen, Honky Tonk, Bill Doggett. They were r-and-b guys who snuck into the pop charts, and I heard – that’s where I heard tenor. Even In the Still of the Night has a great – no, Come Go with Me, my favorite song – the Del Vikings – my favorite song from that era has a great tenor saxophone solo with a giant squeak in the middle of it. I’m either thinking of Come Go with Me or In the Still of…
How about Sam Butera with Louis Prima?

Not at that time, nope, no. There was no jazz – jazz, swing, Benny. None of that was in the house, that I remember, and I didn’t have any relatives. Often you hear, “I went to my uncles, and I heard Benny” [Goodman] – not that I recall.
